info.description: Identity and authorization in one system. Enforcer signs users in, holds who they are (tenants, roles, groups), and answers whether an actor may perform an action on a resource, returning the decision, the policy that made it, and the reason. Because the caller is resolved before evaluation, a policy is handed a real accessor object rather than a bare subject id.
info.title: Enforcer API

All query filters intersect (AND). since/until run on accounts.created_at and are parsed by the same window parser /accounts/summary uses, so the formats and error codes cannot drift between the two endpoints.

post.description: Sets active=true on every id in the body, applying the SAME per-target authorization (ResourceAuth manage, so a tenant_admin can only touch accounts in their own tenant) and the same admin-role-escalation fence as the single-account PUT /accounts/{id}/active. Never all-or-nothing: each id is authorized and applied independently, and the response reports succeeded/failed counts plus a per-id ok|forbidden|error result rather than aborting the batch on the first failure.

Sets active=false on every id in the body — the deactivation twin of bulkActivateAccounts, with the identical per-target authorization, escalation fence, and partial-failure reporting (succeeded/failed counts plus a per-id ok|forbidden|error result). Deactivating does not touch sessions or API keys; combine with bulkInvalidateAccountSessions to force those accounts out immediately.

IRREVERSIBLE. Hard-deletes every id in the body via the same cascade as DELETE /accounts/{id} (Privy user removal, session/key/link revocation, PII scrub, soft-delete) — not a bulk deactivation. Per-target ResourceAuth manage is enforced independently for each id (a tenant_admin can only delete within their own tenant); the response reports succeeded/failed counts and a per-id ok|forbidden|error result, so a partially-authorized batch still deletes everything it was allowed to.

get.description: Typo-tolerant identity search over username, first/last name, email and phone, ranked by pg_trgm trigram similarity. Matches when EITHER the similarity operator fires (typo tolerance, governed by pg_trgm.similarity_threshold) OR q is a plain substring of the haystack OR q exactly equals the account's Privy DID. Row visibility is the identical compiled authz filter GET /accounts uses, so this endpoint cannot surface anything the plain list would hide. Cross-tenant callers (admin) MUST pass tenant_id — omitting it is a 400 tenant_required, never a silent union of every tenant's accounts. Tenant-scoped callers may pass their own tenant_id or omit it.

get.description: One account by id (ResourceAuth read — visible to the account itself, its tenant admins, and platform admins). 404 account_not_found for an unknown or out-of-scope id; the endpoint is not an existence oracle for ids outside the caller's authorized scope.

delete.description: Hard-deletes an account (ResourceAuth manage — admin or tenant_admin only): best-effort removes the upstream Privy user, revokes sessions/API keys/links, scrubs PII, then soft-deletes the row. Irreversible from the API's perspective. For a reversible block use PUT /accounts/{id}/active with active=false instead.

put.description: Flips one account's active flag (ResourceAuth manage). The reversible counterpart to DELETE /accounts/{id}: setting active=false blocks the account without removing data, upstream identity, or history. Returns 403 forbidden if the caller would be escalating an admin account's access, the same fence bulkActivateAccounts/bulkDeactivateAccounts enforce per-target.

get.summary: Passkey MFA status for an account

get.description: Twilio Lookup v2 risk for an account's phone. Self for any authed user; tenant_admin/admin/developer for any account.

put.description: Assigns a role slug to one account (ResourceAuth manage). Rejects with 403 forbidden if the change would escalate an account to admin beyond what the caller may grant, and with 400 unknown_role if the slug does not exist as a role in scope. Role changes take effect immediately — role is read fresh from the account row on every request, never trusted from an old JWT claim.

get.description: Auth-funnel events for one tenant, newest first — including the attempts that never reached an account, which is the whole point. Pass email to answer "did this address ever try, and what failed": the address is hashed server-side and matched against the stored hash, so the search term is never written to the database and the plaintext never had to be stored to be findable. Scoped to the caller's tenant; only a cross-tenant admin may name another via tenant_id. from/to accept RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD. Unknown query parameters are a 400, not a silently unfiltered list.

parameters.name: email

get.description: The CS failed-P2P dashboard: fulfillments across the tenant. Party scope is OPTIONAL: `user_id` matches EITHER side (sender, receiver or creator), while `sender_user_id` / `receiver_user_id` pin one end. All supplied filters intersect, so sender+receiver together mean "from A to B". Without them the list is tenant-wide and only pageable. `status` = closed (cancelled|declined|expired — the failed set), outstanding (pending|claimed|submitted), all, or an exact status. A system admin may pass ?tenant_id to view another tenant; tenant-scoped callers (tenant_admin, developer) are pinned to their own. total matches the rows' filter.

parameters.name: overpaid

get.description: Bucketed counts + notional sums for a single user, for the operator activity chart. `user_id` is matched on EITHER side (sender, receiver or creator) — the same party test GET /admin/fulfillments uses, so the chart and the list it drills into agree about whose transfer a row is. `bucket` is day|week|month. Sent/received split by the CHARTED user's role, not the caller's. `settled` counts only confirmed; `cancelled` folds cancelled|declined|expired and is returned as its OWN series rather than dropped — climbing cancellations are signal. `self_payments` defaults to **exclude**: a self→self fulfillment is funding plumbing, and counting it as customer activity misreads treasury operations as behaviour. Aggregated in SQL, so cost scales with buckets rather than transfers.

get.description: Operator point lookup for a transfer named in a ticket. Fenced to the caller's tenant (or `tenant_id` for the admin role): an id in another tenant is a 404, never a 403, so the endpoint is not an existence oracle. Counterparty contact PII is scrubbed — the operator is not a party.

Platform-wide search over PERSONS (the cross-tenant human identity that accounts hang off), not accounts — requires the cross-tenant grant. This is how you find every account one human holds across tenants and spot a duplicate signup; an account-level search cannot see across tenant boundaries. tenant_id restricts to persons with a live account in that tenant; invited_by restricts to persons with an account invited by a given account id.

parameters.description: restrict to persons with a live account in this tenant
parameters.name: tenant_id

parameters.description: restrict to persons with an account invited by this account id
parameters.name: invited_by

get.description: One person's platform-wide record: identity fields and every account they hold, across every tenant. Requires the cross-tenant grant, same as listPersons.

delete.description: Cascading soft-delete of a cross-tenant PERSON, not a single account. A tenant_admin caller only removes that person's membership in the ADMIN'S OWN tenant — other tenants' accounts for the same person survive untouched; a system-admin (cross_tenant) caller deletes the person platform-wide. reason is optional and recorded for audit.

patch.description: Partial PII patch on a cross-tenant person: a field present in the JSON body is applied — even an empty string clears it — while an absent field is left unchanged, so a {} body is a no-op. username is rejected with 400 (it is account-scoped, not person-scoped; use PATCH /accounts/{id} instead). The regulated block — DOB, home address, primary email and phone — is echoed back in the response only to a system-admin (global) caller, never to a tenant_admin, so an empty patch cannot be used as a read of those fields at the lower gate.

parameters.description: referrer username / email (substring) or account id (exact)
parameters.name: q

get.description: Every role in the catalog, built-in and custom — roles are a global table with no tenant_id, so this is not tenant-scoped. Gated on tenant_read or above; see also listRoles (GET /roles), the same underlying data exposed to ANY authenticated caller with no admin gate, for populating a role picker.

post.description: Creates a custom role with an arbitrary permission grant. System-admin (platform-only) gated — there is no separate escalation fence because only a caller who already holds cross_tenant (the maximum grant) can reach this route at all. slug must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{1,49}$ (mixed case is lowercased, not rejected) and may not collide with a built-in slug (admin, tenant_admin, developer, user), which returns 409.

get.description: One role by id, including its full permission grant (cross_tenant, tenant_read, tenant_write, tenant_manage, admin_managed).

put.description: Updates a custom role's name, description, or permission grant (each field optional; permissions, if present, REPLACES the full set rather than merging individual flags). Built-in roles return 409 immutable. System-admin (platform-only) gated, for the same reason as createRole: only a cross_tenant holder can reach this route.

delete.description: Deletes a CUSTOM role only — built-in slugs (admin, tenant_admin, developer, user) return 409 conflict, as does a role still assigned to any account (reassign those accounts first). System-admin (platform-only) gated.

get.description: The CS bank-link dashboard: client telemetry from the Plaid link + bank-exchange flows (source IN plaid_link, bank_link_exchange, external_bank_unlink). An explicit `source` query overrides the default set; `event` (e.g. EXIT) narrows further. Same tenant scoping and retention as the general feed.

parameters.description: CSV override of the default bank-link sources
parameters.name: source

get.description: Every version this tenant has submitted, newest first, whatever became of it — including the rejected ones and the reason each was refused.

post.description: Stores a new version of the caller's tenant policy and validates it. A REJECTED submission is stored too, with the reason: "what did I send that you refused" is the first question support gets, and by then the author no longer has the draft. Validation compiles the Rego against a restricted capability set (no network, no process environment, nothing non-deterministic), checks the package namespace, and runs the policy's own test_ rules. A refused policy still returns 200 — the submission succeeded, the policy failed — with the verdict in `validation`.

get.description: Which accounts in the caller's tenant have their own policy active, which version, and since when. Deliberately NOT the source: an account's policy is the rules that account put on itself, and oversight — knowing one is in force, and being able to switch it off — does not need the text. An account policy can only narrow its own account, so nothing in it can widen anyone's access.
get.summary: Account policies in force in this tenant

delete.description: Retires the active policy of an account in the caller's tenant. The account then answers to platform and tenant policy alone — which is where it would be had it never written one, so this can only return an account to access its role and the tenant's policy already allow. The account keeps its version history and can activate a version again; to stop that, change its role or the tenant's policy. An account outside the caller's tenant is not found by construction: the tenant comes from the credential, never the request.
delete.summary: Switch off one account's own policy

get.description: Returns the tenant's active policy, or null when it has none — which is every tenant until they write one, and so is a 200 with null data rather than a 404.

delete.description: Leaves the tenant with no policy. Platform resource types then fall back to platform policy alone; any type the retired policy DECLARED is denied, because no policy is no authority. Rolling back to an earlier version is an activate, not a deactivate — every version is still there.

get.description: The source as submitted, its status, and — when it was refused — the validation error. This is what an author opens after a rejection, and what an operator opens when asked why something was denied on a given day.

post.description: Promotes a validated version and retires whatever was active, then announces it so every pod stops evaluating the previous one. Refuses a version that has not passed validation: activating an unvalidated policy turns a compile error into a tenant-wide outage at request time instead of a rejection at submit time.
post.summary: Make a tenant policy version live

get.description: Live identity-provider state for one account beside enforcer's own row: the account's stored email/phone and their verified flags, the VERIFIED contacts Privy holds right now, whether they still agree, and the live passkey MFA posture. email_matches_account is the field to read first — a Privy-linked address that has drifted from accounts.email sends every login code to an inbox the user no longer reads, and nothing else in the database exposes that. Both match fields are null (never false) when either side is blank, since "Privy holds no email" is a different problem from "the emails disagree"; both values ship in the body so a null always explains itself. privy is null for an account with no Privy user (native/SSO tenants), which is a fact about the tenant, not a fault. A Privy read that fails refuses the whole response rather than serving it with the provider half silently missing.
get.summary: Privy identity state for an account

parameters.description: tenant_id assertion — 404s when it does not match the account's tenant
parameters.name: tenant_id

get.description: Admin-read of ONE account's verification sessions (one row per provider and type), carrying the same server-computed `can_retry`, `blocked_reason` and `remedy` the account owner sees. `can_retry` is the gate a client should branch on — never re-derive it from `status`, which gets `expired` and `failed` wrong (both are retryable; only a customer-level rejection is terminal) and reports a verified account as blocked. `blocked_reason` is `customer_rejected` (only the provider's compliance team can lift it), `already_verified` (a SUCCESS, not a block), or absent. Tenant-scoped: naming an account in another tenant is 403 `account_not_in_tenant`, not 404, so the id space cannot be probed — a system admin with cross_tenant reads any tenant.

The custody drift worklist: accounts whose LIVE signing posture does not match what our rows claim. Open findings only unless include_resolved=true. Ordered worst-and-oldest first (critical before warning, then by how long the condition has persisted).

post.description: Threads an ALREADY-EXISTING quorum-owned Privy wallet into account_wallets as the account's multisig wallet, and makes it primary. For wallets minted outside v3 (a migration spike, or by hand during an incident) — those are invisible on the Privy user object, so no automatic path can discover them, and the ensure path would mint a duplicate instead of adopting. The wallet's live owner quorum is VERIFIED to be a true 2-of-2 naming this account's Privy user before anything is written; a mistyped wallet id is refused rather than recorded. Refuses when the account already records a multisig wallet.
post.summary: Adopt an existing Privy wallet as the account's 2-of-2 wallet

get.description: Machine credentials visible to the caller: their own keys, or — for a tenant admin — every key issued in their tenant. The plaintext secret is never returned here or anywhere after creation; only id, name, key_prefix, active and last_used_at are exposed.

post.description: Mints a new API key for the CALLER's own account and returns the plaintext exactly once in this response — it is never retrievable again. name is required and cannot be blank: an unnamed key is a working credential nobody can identify to revoke later, so an empty or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 missing_fields rather than silently minting an anonymous key. scope is optional and space-delimited, in the same vocabulary OAuth grants (enforcer:read | enforcer:write | enforcer:admin | policy:self | enforcer:<tag>.<effect>); the key stores it and the response echoes it. A key never exceeds its owner's role and permissions, and a scope narrows it further. A caller whose own credential carries a scope may only mint at or below it (the coarse ladder read < write < admin; a fine scope is covered by its own tag at an equal-or-wider effect or by a covering coarse scope) and is refused with 403 insufficient_scope otherwise; such a caller that omits scope gets a key carrying its own scope, never an unscoped one. An unscoped caller (a login session, an unscoped API key) may mint any scope or none. An unknown scope is 400 invalid_scope.

delete.description: Hard-removes an API key row (ResourceAuth write — the key's own account, or a tenant admin over their tenant's keys). Unlike Revoke, this does not leave an inactive row for audit; prefer POST /api-keys/{id}/revoke when the goal is to disable the credential while keeping a record it existed. 404 key_not_found for an unknown or out-of-scope id.

get.description: The audit trail, newest first, filter-scoped by role: admin sees every tenant, tenant_admin sees only their own tenant, everyone else sees nothing (not even their own actions — use GET /me/audit-events instead). from/to accept RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD; a malformed bound is a 400, not a silently ignored filter. session_id matches EITHER the enforcer refresh-token family (session_id) or the upstream provider's session (external_session_id, e.g. a Privy sid), so one query finds every audit event from one login regardless of which id space logged it.

parameters.description: one login's events — matches session_id (enforcer refresh-token family) OR external_session_id (the provider's, e.g. a Privy sid)
parameters.name: session_id

get.description: Counts over the SAME compiled row filter and from/to window semantics as GET /audit-events (including the RFC3339-or-YYYY-MM-DD parsing and malformed-bound-is-400 rule), so a summary tile never claims a count the event list itself would refuse to show. group_by is one of action, resource_type or actor (actor buckets NULL actor_account_id — system-initiated events like verification grants — under the explicit key "system" rather than leaving it blank); interval adds a time-bucketed data.series over the same window.

parameters.description: hour | day | week | month — returns data.series
parameters.name: interval

parameters.description: one login's events — matches session_id OR external_session_id
parameters.name: session_id

parameters.name: tz

get.description: Public: given an optional `tenant_code`, reports how that tenant's login UI should authenticate — native OTP/passkey/SIWE vs. Privy custom auth — plus the tenant's public `privy_app_id` (never a secret) so the client can initialize the right SDK before the user picks a method.
The push providers configured on this deployment (e.g. FCM/APNs), for a client choosing which provider code to pass to registerDevice.

Public, rate-limited: given `email` (and optional `tenant_code`), reports whether an account with that address already exists and is verified WITHIN THAT ONE TENANT, so a signup UI can route to login vs. register vs. "email taken" without leaking whether the address is registered in any other tenant. `email` must parse as a bare address (no display-name form, no dotless domain) or the call is a 400 `invalid_email`, distinct from the 200 `exists:false` a well-formed-but-unregistered address returns.

post.description: The authenticated caller redeems an invite token and gains the membership it grants. 410 invite_invalid if the token is expired, already used, or cancelled; 403 email_mismatch if the invite was addressed to a different email than the caller's verified identity; 403 wallet_mismatch if the invite was addressed to a different wallet.

Authenticates a credential and, on success, issues an enforcer access/refresh token pair (200, `handler.AuthResponse`). `provider` in the request selects the scheme and its required fields: `email_otp` needs `email`+`code`, `phone_otp` needs `phone`+`code`, `siwe` needs `message`+`signature`, every other provider needs `token` (e.g. a Privy access token). 401 on a rejected credential or wrong/expired OTP, 403 `account_inactive` for a deactivated account or `wrong_auth_scheme` when the tenant requires a different provider, 404 when no tenant matches the credential, 409 only on a benign concurrent-refresh race elsewhere in the family, 503 when the upstream identity provider (Privy/Google) is unreachable.
Revokes the caller's entire refresh-token family (all devices/sessions sharing that `refresh_token`'s lineage), given `refresh_token` in the body. 401 if the token doesn't resolve to the caller.

get.description: The authenticated caller's own identity in one call: account (id, tenant, role, wallet address, login/activity timestamps), permissions, verification sessions plus the derived KYC-verified flag, resolved authz groups (id/slug/name), inline terms-acceptance posture, the caller's referral code, and — for a send-enforced tenant with a smart wallet not yet migrated — a `wallet_send_migration_required` flag. Terms and referral data are best-effort: a lookup hiccup on either omits that field rather than failing the whole call.

post.description: Register or refresh a push-capable device under the caller's person: provider + push_token are required, plus device_id/device_name, os_name/os_version, app_identifier/app_version, and — for signed push — public_key/key_algorithm, with free-form metadata. An unknown provider code is 400 unknown_provider.

Refuses more than is refundable: what actually arrived (routed settlements) minus refunds already live or confirmed against it, checked under a lock on the original so two refunds cannot each claim the full balance. The refusal carries `refundable_uoa`.

Records that the service broadcast the payout for reward fulfillment `id` from its treasury wallet: `pending` → `submitted` with `tx_hash`, then a best-effort settlement attempt from that transaction's receipt (the enforcer-reconcile sweep retries it regardless).

**Reward rows only.** The row must belong to `X-Tenant-ID` (404 otherwise — existence is not revealed across tenants) and its reference must carry the `RWD:` tag (403 `not_a_reward_fulfillment`); a service key cannot stamp a P2P, bill-pay or POS row.

**Idempotent.** A row that already carries this same hash — `submitted`, or `confirmed` because the Routed webhook got there first — answers 200 with the current row. A confirmed row with no hash is stamped with this one. A different hash is 409 `tx_hash_conflict`; an expired/declined/cancelled/failed row is 409 `not_pending`.

Settlement: a route-rail payout confirms from its `Routed(memo)` event as today. A send-rail payout (plain ERC-20 `transfer`) confirms from the Transfer log in this transaction whose token is `request_token`, recipient `receiver_wallet` and value at least `notional_uoa`.
Submit a support message. Creates a support ticket and emails the tenant's support inbox; the returned ticket_id resolves at GET /tickets/{id}.

Unauthenticated ingest for auth-funnel events from callers with no account context yet — the population that cannot emit ordinary client telemetry. event must be one of otp_requested, otp_send_failed, otp_verify_failed, login_failed; anything else is a 400 rather than a stored row, because a free-text event on an unauthenticated write would let anyone mint rows a support feed then displays as fact. The email is stored HASHED (for lookup) and MASKED (for reading), never in the clear. Well-formed requests answer 202 whether or not a row was written — an unknown tenant_code is dropped silently so this cannot be used to probe which tenant codes exist. Per-IP rate limited.

Ingests one client diagnostic event from the calling app (PWA/mobile). Fire-and-forget: returns 202 immediately — the structured server log is the primary record, this table only backs the admin read endpoints. source and event are both required in the body; an event with either blank is rejected 400.

get.description: Tenants visible to the caller: a platform admin sees every tenant, a tenant admin sees their own, anyone else sees none. q searches name or code; status filters active/inactive/suspended. Each tenant's code (the join secret) is present only for a platform admin or that tenant's own tenant_admin — every other caller gets it stripped to null, not omitted.

post.description: Provisions a new tenant. System-admin only — 403 for any other caller, since there is no existing tenant row yet for a resource-level check to apply to.

Creates a tenant (workspace) owned by the caller's person, who becomes its `tenant_admin`; returns tokens scoped to the new tenant. 403 `self_serve_disabled` when self-serve creation is off on this instance. 403 `workspace_limit_reached` when workspace-plan enforcement is on and the caller already owns as many live workspaces as their plan allows (the message states the allowed and owned counts; `getSelfServeTenantAllowance` returns both). Only workspaces the caller created through this endpoint count — being `tenant_admin` of someone else's tenant uses no slot.

get.description: Returns the caller's workspace plan (projected from enforcer-billing), the effective number of workspaces they may own (`workspace_slots` — the instance default when billing has not projected a plan for them), how many live workspaces they own (`owned`), and whether the limit is enforced on this instance (`enforced`). Read-only. Only workspaces created through `selfServeTenant` count as owned.

One metric row per tenant the caller may read: accounts, active accounts, KYC-verified accounts, groups, pending invites and last signup — the platform-console view that replaces a list-then-N-counts loop. Scoped by the SAME compiled row filter as GET /tenants, so a tenant admin sees exactly their own tenant's row and a platform admin sees every tenant; a non-admin caller simply gets one row (their own), never an error.

One tenant's full configuration: branding, app/payment-link URLs, auth and wallet provider, join policy, status. code (the join secret) is redacted to null unless the caller is a platform admin or that tenant's own tenant_admin — same redaction rule as listTenants.

delete.description: Soft-deletes a tenant. System-admin only. Irreversible in the sense that PATCH {status:"inactive"} — a reversible deactivation — is almost certainly what you want instead.

patch.description: Partial update of tenant configuration (branding, URLs, join policy, status, etc.) — only fields present in the body change. Behind a manage-level resource check (tenant admins may update their own tenant; platform admins any tenant).

post.description: Replaces the tenant's join code with a freshly generated one and returns it in the response body (the only time the new value is shown in full). The OLD code stops working immediately for anyone trying to join with it — every join link and any invite text that embeds the old code goes stale, so this is a "the help-desk is about to get join-code tickets" action, not a routine rotation.

get.description: List the tenant's invites. Callers with tenant authority see all invites; regular members see only the ones they sent.

post.description: Invite an email or wallet address into the tenant. Provide exactly one of email or wallet_address. Any member of the tenant may send an invite; callers without tenant authority always invite at the "user" role (passing another role returns 403). A wallet invite admits that address on first SIWE login of an invite-only tenant.

get.description: Visibility mirrors GET /tenants/{id}/invites EXACTLY: caller-scoped to invites they sent by default, tenant-wide only with all=true from a manage-role caller. That asymmetry is an email-PII boundary — a summary that counted tenant-wide rows for a self-scoped caller would disclose how many invites other people sent, and its total would contradict the list it drills into. status filters pending|accepted|expired|cancelled; email is a case-insensitive substring match.

delete.description: Cancels a pending invite before it is accepted — an already-accepted, expired, or already-cancelled invite is a 404, not a no-op. Behind the tenant manage gate (developer role and up); a plain member who SENT the invite cannot cancel it themselves.

put.description: Replaces the tenant's HALO-Lego module entitlements — which product surfaces this tenant has BOUGHT (V3-02). Values are group slugs prefixed `module_` (`module_work`, `module_money`); the prefix is required, because after these are unioned into the accessor's group slugs it is the only thing separating them from identity groups like `contractor`. A REPLACE, not a patch: send the full desired set. **System-admin only** — a tenant_admin passes the route's manage check but must not be able to grant their own tenant a module, which is writing their own invoice. Every leaf's entitlement gate fails CLOSED, so removing a module closes those surfaces on the next resolve.

get.description: Every terms document row the caller may read (admin: all; tenant admin: their tenant's + global), including inactive and expired versions — this is the admin history view, not the "what applies right now" view (that's getMyTerms). Unfiltered beyond role scope: no type/active/tenant query params exist yet.

post.description: Creates a NEW terms document version. This does NOT deactivate or supersede any existing active version of the same type — setTermsActive is a separate, explicit step. Until the old version is turned off, getMyTerms' current-version resolution treats both as active and picks between them (tenant-specific over global, otherwise the newest-effective), so a caller may keep seeing the version they already accepted. content_hash is computed server-side (sha256 of content) and is what an acceptance snapshots, not a client-supplied value. tenant_id is admin-only; a tenant_admin caller is silently pinned to their own tenant regardless of what they pass.

get.description: One terms document by id. Cross-tenant and unauthorized reads collapse to 404, not 403 — a foreign tenant's document id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent one, so this is never a cross-tenant existence oracle.

put.description: Flips one document's is_active flag. There is no enforced "one active version per type" invariant — activating a new version leaves any previously-active version of the same type active too, and deactivating a still-accepted mandatory document silently drops the onboarding gate for everyone who was blocked on it. A tenant admin may only toggle documents owned by their own tenant; global (tenant_id null) documents are admin-only, since toggling one changes the gate for every tenant at once.

Support staff (a `tenant_read` holder in the tenant, i.e. the `developer` role and up) may pass `requester_account_id` to open the ticket ON BEHALF OF another account in the same tenant — the agent-on-a-call path. The ticket then belongs to that customer, so `GET /tickets?requester=` finds it and the customer's own owner-baseline read can see it; the first message is still authored by the agent who typed it. A non-staff caller passing someone else's id gets 403, and an unknown or cross-tenant id gets 400.

get.description: The caller's person-level verifications (KYC packets, attestations), cross-tenant by construction because they hang off the person, not the account. Self-scoped: a filter narrows this set and can never reach another person's rows. With NO query string the response is the legacy `{success, data:[...], count}` shape, every row, submitted_at DESC — unchanged. With `limit` or `offset` the response is the ADR 0003 envelope `{success, data:{items, total, filtered, limit, offset}}`; `limit=0` returns counts alone. Filters or a sort WITHOUT `limit`/`offset` return the legacy shape over the filtered, sorted rows. `status`/`kind`/`issuer` are comma-separated ORs; an unrecognised member matches nothing. `q` is a case-insensitive substring over id, issuer and decision_reason — the row only; the person is not searched because the list is already one person's. `from`/`to` bound the column named by `date_field` (default submitted_at): `YYYY-MM-DD` is an inclusive whole UTC day, RFC3339 an exact instant (`to` exclusive); a row with no value in that column is excluded when a bound is set and included otherwise. `since`/`until` and `created_after`/`created_before` are aliases. Nullable sort columns (decided, expires) order NULLS LAST in both directions; every sort tiebreaks on id. An unknown query KEY is `400 unknown_param`.

is_discoverable.description:
IsDiscoverable gates whether this account can be added as a linked contact
by others in the same tenant. Defaults true (see migration 000022).

passkey_mfa_verified_at.description:
PasskeyMfaVerifiedAt stamps when the SERVER observed, via the Privy
management API, that this account's passkey MFA enrollment is complete
(factor advertised + a linked credential backing it). NULL = never
verified. Written only by SetPasskeyMfaVerified from the
/auth/me/passkey/verify flow — the client's own view of Privy state is
eventually consistent and must never be the source of this stamp.

provisioned_via.description:
ProvisionedVia is how this membership came to exist (migration 000088):
ProvisionedViaPortalToken marks a SHELL ACCOUNT minted by a cold portal
link; nil is an ordinary signup (every row that predates the column).
ClaimedAt is when a verified login by the same person bound a credential
to a shell; nil on an unclaimed shell and on every non-shell row.

wallet_send_migrated_at.description:
WalletSendMigratedAt stamps when this account's smart wallet had the
mandatory app-key owner quorum attached (wallet-send-enforcement). NULL =
not yet migrated; the login-heal signals the PWA to prompt for the
one-time owner-change authorization when the tenant is send-enforced.

scope.description:
Scope narrows what the key may do below its owner's grant. nil is the
only value existing keys carry and means unnarrowed — the key acts with
the account's full permissions, exactly as before the column existed.
Omitted from JSON when nil, so a response for an unscoped key is
byte-identical to what it was.

external_session_id.description:
ExternalSessionID is the identity PROVIDER's session (Privy's `sid`),
populated only when the actor authenticated with a raw provider token and
therefore holds no enforcer session (migration 000071). Exactly one of
SessionID / ExternalSessionID is ever set; both nil means the credential
has no session at all (API key, portal link, service principal, worker).

It is deliberately NOT merged into SessionID: that column joins to
refresh_tokens, and a provider session never will.

session_id.description:
SessionID is the login session the actor was acting under (migration
000069). Callers do not set it: Record fills it from the request context,
so every emitter gets session attribution without knowing sessions exist.

Nil is normal and carries meaning — the action was taken with a credential
that is not a session (API key, portal link, raw provider bearer, service
principal) or by a background worker. Do not read nil as "unknown".

account_id.description:
AccountID is NULL for the normal case — a caller who cannot log in has no
account context. It is populated only where the server could resolve one
anyway, and its absence is never an error.

email_masked.description:
EmailMasked is enough to recognize an address in a feed, not enough to be
an address list if the table leaks.

config.description:
Config is the decrypted credential map — populated only on authorized
single-row reads, never on lists.

provider_app_id.description:
ProviderAppID is the provider's PUBLIC application id (e.g. the Privy app id).
Plaintext (not in the sealed config) so it can be queried for login tenant
resolution and served to the client SDK. app_secret stays in config_encrypted.

send_enforcement.description:
SendEnforcement marks this connection's tenant as wallet-send-enforced
(multi-sig): the tenant's Privy smart wallets get the mandatory app-key
owner quorum and rwa's signing gateway enforces send policy. It lives on
the connection row — the mode is baggage of the cybrid-bank wiring for
specific tenants, not a property of every Privy tenant. Plaintext (not in
the sealed config) so operators flip it with one UPDATE. A tenant is
enforced iff ANY active connection row carries the flag; when rotating the
flagged connection, set it on the replacement row or enforcement drops.

alerts.description:
Alerts is a computed field populated on list/get for LINKED contacts: the
caller's unacked fulfillment (send/receive) tallies with that contact,
read from enforcer-cybrid and keyed on the shared account id. Best-effort —
nil when the fulfillment service is unconfigured or unreachable, or when
the contact has no outstanding activity. Acks happen against cybrid; this
is read-only badge data. Never stored.

avatar_url.description:
AvatarURL is the resolved picture the client should render: the owner's
CustomAvatarURL override when set, else the linked person's own
profile_image_url. Computed on list/get so the PWA has ONE field to read
and never has to implement the precedence itself. Never stored.

custom_avatar_url.description:
CustomAvatarURL is the OWNER's private picture override for this contact
(migration 000057). Meaningful on both contact types: on a linked contact
it shadows the linked person's own profile_image_url, on a custom contact
it is the only picture there is. nil = no override.

custom_wallet_address.description:
CustomWalletAddress is a manually-entered pay-to wallet on a custom contact
(custom contacts have no account to derive WalletAddress from). Ported from
v2; only custom contacts ever set it.

favorite_rank.description:
FavoriteRank orders the owner's favorite contacts: nil = not favorited,
1 = first favorite. A user may hold MANY favorites — the rank is a
per-owner ordering, not a single slot (unique per owner among non-null
ranks, see migration 000056). Favorites float to the top of every list.

username.description:
FirstName/LastName/Email are computed display fields populated by the
contacts usecase on list/get: for linked contacts from the contact's
account, for custom contacts mirrored from the custom_* columns. This
gives the PWA one uniform name/email shape per row (matching the legacy
contacts list) without a second lookup. Never stored.
Username is the linked contact's account handle (@username), populated on
list/get so the PWA can show @handle instead of falling back to email.
Custom contacts have no account, so it stays nil. Never stored.

wallet_address.description:
WalletAddress is a computed field populated by the contacts usecase for
linked contacts — the embedded wallet of the contact's account. Never
stored in the contacts table; loaded from accounts on list/get.

public_key.description:
PublicKey is the base64 Ed25519 key the device signs check-ins with,
trusted on first registration (TOFU). KeyAlgorithm names the scheme.

delivered.description:
Delivered is base units of Token, read from the receipt's Transfer logs
(the chain publishes it nowhere else). Empty when not resolved.

delivery_legs.description:
DeliveryLegs is what the RECEIVER got, which no on-chain event reports —
see migration 000077. Neither Routed nor GPVRecorded carries an output
token or amount, and the Router's per-leg distribution emits nothing, so
this is resolved from Book.getPlan plus the receipt's Transfer logs.

PlanVerified gates it: only TRUE means our re-hash matched the event's
planHash and the legs are exact. FALSE means inferred (the plan changed
under us, or an unrecoverable inlinePlan) and NULL means never attempted.
Neither is "probably fine" — 25.6% of settled rows on prod were paid under
a plan that has since changed, because a receiver can rewrite their own
plan at will (Book.setPlan is ungated on msg.sender).

expected_payer_wallet.description:
ExpectedPayerWallet, when set, is the ONLY wallet that may fund this
fulfillment — see PayerBound and migration 000101. Never inferred from an
account and never backfilled from whoever paid; sender_wallet is the
snapshot/observed field and this is the RULE.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey de-duplicates CREATE (migration 000082). Optional: when a
caller supplies one, a second create with the same (tenant_id, key)
returns the ORIGINAL row instead of minting a second payment. Unique per
tenant over non-NULL values, for the row's whole lifetime — a retry that
arrives after the original settled must still resolve to it, which is
exactly the "answer lost, client retried later" case.

kind.description:
Kind is the product line this fulfillment belongs to: p2p | deposit |
billpay | direct | reward. Derived server-side from the reference tag at
create (ClassifyKind) and stored, rather than re-derived per query from a
free-text column. Empty only on rows written before migration 000075 or by
a pod still on the previous image; the query layer falls back to the
reference for those.

memo.description: bytes32 on-chain memo — the join key between this record and chain state.

paid_uoa.description:
PaidUOA is the summed ROUTED settlements for this row's memo — what
actually arrived, against NotionalUOA's what-was-owed. The excess is
PaidUOA - NotionalUOA, and it is the reason this field exists: the
overpaid filter finds rows where a payer routed the same memo twice or a
route declared more than the request asked for, but a boolean cannot tell
support HOW MUCH.

DERIVED, not a column (gorm:"-"): computed per page by the admin read
paths. A POINTER because absent must stay distinguishable from zero — on
any endpoint that does not compute it, a plain string would render "0",
which reads as "nothing ever arrived" for a fully paid transfer.

refunded_uoa.description:
RefundedUOA is how much has actually been refunded AGAINST this payment:
the summed routed settlements of every refund naming it. Same shape and
the same reason as PaidUOA — a boolean "refunded" cannot answer "how
much", and partial refunds are the normal case.

A POINTER because absent must stay distinguishable from zero: on an
endpoint that does not compute it, a plain string would render "0", which
reads as "never refunded" for a fully refunded payment.

refunds_fulfillment_id.description:
RefundsFulfillmentID is the payment this one REVERSES, parsed from the
reference. Derived, not a column: the reference is the record, and a
second stored copy could disagree with it.

sender.description: Populated by the usecase for authenticated endpoints — never stored.

sender_cost_uoa.description:
SenderCostUOA is value_at_mid(input_spent_actual) - notional_uoa: what the
route cost the sender ABOVE what was delivered. fee_charged is only part
of it — on the Aug-26 route the fee was 2.99 USDC and the true cost 13.18.

SlippageUOA is the residual after the fee. ★ It is NOT always "lost": on a
DIRECT same-token leg the principal never swaps, so the gap is a transfer
to the RECEIVER rather than a loss to liquidity providers. Check
DeliveryLegs before calling it a loss. Negative means the route beat mid,
and it is stored signed so a better-than-mid execution is not clamped away.

NULL means NOT COMPUTED — no pool for the input token, an RPC failure, or
a row predating migration 000081. It never means zero.

bucket.description: Bucket is the period start, RFC3339 date (day/week) or month start.

cancelled_count.description: Cancelled folds cancelled | declined | expired — ended without payment.

sent_count.description: Sent / Received count every non-cancelled row in the period.

settled_count.description: Settled is the subset that actually moved money (status = confirmed).

is_contact.description:
IsContact is true when this counterparty is already a saved (linked)
contact of the caller viewing the row, so the PWA can badge it without a
second lookup. Computed per-viewer; false for the caller themselves.

wallet_address.description:
WalletAddress is the counterparty's on-file wallet (from their account),
so the row renders the send/receive wallet alongside the name.

group_type_id.description:
GroupTypeID classifies the group; nil = untyped. Must reference a GLOBAL
type or one from the group's own tenant (enforced by the usecase).

member_count.description: MemberCount is computed on load, not stored.

group_count.description:
GroupCount is how many live groups use this type — computed on list
reads (read-only column), never stored. The console used to pull 500
groups to count per type client-side; wrong past 500, wasteful before.

metadata.description:
Metadata carries client presentation hints (icon, color, ordering …);
the server never interprets it.

email.description: Email is the invited inbox. Empty on wallet-only invites (SIWE agents).

wallet_address.description:
WalletAddress is the invited EVM address, stored lowercase. Empty on
email-only invites. Exactly one of Email / WalletAddress is set.

acceptance_rate.description:
AcceptanceRate is Accepted / Resolved as a percentage, 1dp.

Deliberately NOT accepted/total: a tenant that just sent 100 invites would
otherwise show ~0% acceptance purely because they are all still pending,
which reads as failure rather than as "too early to say". Zero when nothing
has resolved yet.

resolved.description:
Resolved is the count of invites that reached a terminal state
(accepted + expired + cancelled), i.e. total minus still-pending.

person_deleted.description:
PersonDeleted is false when the person row was KEPT because they still
hold live accounts in other tenants. A tenant-scoped delete removes the
membership, not the human.

home_place_id.description:
Home address — canonical, owned here (cybrid KYC + report-builder read it).
HomePlaceID references an enforcer-geo place; the rest is a denormalized
snapshot so /auth/me serves the address without a geo round-trip.

decided_at.description:
Decision fields populate together when an admin approves or rejects.
DecidedBy FKs back to accounts.id — "which admin made the call" is an
audit-trail concern, not an identity one.

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt lets the background expiry job age out stale approvals (e.g. a
1-year KYC). Nil = no expiry policy for this row.

file_id.description:
FileID is a cross-service reference into enforcer-files (files moved out
of the enforcer in v3), so there is no local FK. Pointer because not every
verification has an attached document (issuer-attested booleans, on-chain
proofs, etc.).

issuer.description:
Issuer is the third party that produced the attestation. "self" for
user-submitted docs awaiting admin review.

kind.description:
Kind is intentionally a free-form varchar (not an enum) so adding a new
verification type doesn't require a migration. Operator policy lives at
the usecase layer.

metadata.description:
Metadata is a free-form JSON bag for issuer-specific fields (document
type, sanctions-screen score, etc.).

kyc_verified.description:
KycVerified is, of those, how many hold a verified kyc/kyb verification
session — the ONLY number user-facing invite counters should render
(product rule: invite friends counts KYC'd users, never raw signups).

referred.description: accounts whose invited_by is this account

cross_tenant.description: Capability grants (additive; all false = baseline-only, like "user").

config.description:
Config is the decrypted configuration — populated only on authorized
single-row reads (with secret fields redacted), never on lists.

slug.description:
Slug is the human-friendly handle for the unauthenticated flow routes
(/auth/sso/:connection/...). Globally unique among live rows — the flow
resolves a connection with no tenant in hand. IdP-registered URLs
(redirect_uri / ACS / entity id) always use the UUID so renames never
break federation.

last_signup_at.description: LastSignupAt is the newest account created_at, nil for an empty tenant.

verified.description:
Verified counts ACCOUNTS with a verified kyc/kyb session, not sessions —
the same predicate the contacts KYC gate and referral stats use, so the
console and the gate agree on who is verified.

auth_provider.description: AuthProvider / WalletProvider: nil = inherit the instance default.

billing_status.description:
BillingStatus is the tenant's platform-billing dunning state, PROJECTED
from enforcer-billing (migration 000087): "" | active | past_due |
restricted | suspended | collections. enforcer-billing is the source of
truth; this is a copy the billing.status_changed consumer keeps current so
the value rides Accessor.billing_status on every resolve with no hop.

"" means UNKNOWN and readers MUST treat it as active (fail open).

`<-:false` makes GORM never write these two columns: Repository.Update is
a whole-row Save, so without it an admin editing the tenant's name from a
stale struct would silently roll the projection back. Only
BillingStatusStore.ApplyBillingStatus writes them, by targeted UPDATE
under the monotonic entered_at guard.

metadata.description: Metadata is a generic per-tenant jsonb bag (feature flags, extension config).

metered_sends_enabled.description:
MeteredSendsEnabled turns on per-transaction limit metering: every value leg
leaving the platform is measured against the caller's live cap before the
server co-signs. Meaningful only while Web3Enabled is true — the pair
(false, true) is refused on write; see ValidateWeb3Gates.

modules.description:
Modules is the tenant's MODULE entitlements as group slugs, prefixed
`module_` (migration 000094, V3-02). Which HALO-Lego surfaces this tenant
has bought — NOT which of them any given account may use, which is the
role's question.

It lives on the tenant rather than in account_groups because it is a fact
about the TENANT: a module per account would mean auto-joining every new
account and would make "remove one person from a module the tenant paid
for" expressible. The resolver UNIONS this into Accessor.GroupSlugs, so
every leaf's RequireModule reads it with no new field and no extra hop.

Same `<-:false` guard and the same targeted-write rule as BillingStatus
above: Repository.Update is a whole-row Save, so without it an admin
editing the tenant's name from a stale struct would silently revoke every
module. Only ModuleStore writes these two columns.

theme_colors.description:
ThemeColors is the tenant's colour palette — a `jsonb` column that has
existed since the identity schema (000001) and was never wired to a model
field, so nothing has ever read or written it.

It stays a loose map because the column is genuinely untyped and the KEY
VOCABULARY is not defined yet: EPIC-002 RN-01 owns it, since the render
module is the first real consumer and the set a PDF needs is the set worth
agreeing on. Giving it a struct here would assert a shape the column does
not enforce and no writer produces.

web3_enabled.description:
Web3Enabled is the tenant-wide web3 kill switch. False rejects EVERY web3
transaction for the tenant — guarded sends, signing, and RPC writes alike —
so it is deliberately a gate rather than an enforcement mode. Defaults true
(migration 000066) because false would disable web3 for every existing
tenant on deploy.

declared_types.description:
DeclaredTypes are the resource types this policy is authoritative for.
Platform types are never here: on those a tenant policy may only DENY,
never widen. On a declared type, no policy means no authority.

source.description: Source is the Rego verbatim as submitted.

source_sha256.description:
SourceSHA256 lets a re-submit of identical text be recognised as a no-op
rather than minting a version that changes nothing.

subject_account_id.description:
SubjectAccountID is set when the policy governs one account rather than
the tenant. See Subject.

version.description:
Version is monotonic per subject and never reused, because it is what a
decision log cites and what an evaluator's cache keys on.

file_ids.description:
FileIDs are enforcer-files ids. Persisted now; the presigned-URL broker
that makes them readable cross-user is Phase 2 (docs/plans/ticket-api.md).

internal.description:
Internal marks a staff-only note: never shown to the requester, never
notifies. The usecase fences both writing and reading it to staff.

external_key.description:
ExternalKey is the FILING SYSTEM's own id for the thing this ticket is
about — a payment id, a refund id — set only when a service raised it.

It exists because Kafka is at-least-once: a redelivered message, a DLQ
replay or two consumer replicas racing would each open a fresh ticket for
one payout, and three copies of a problem is worse than none — the second
agent works a ticket the first already answered. Unique per tenant
(partial index, migration 000090), so a re-file returns the existing row.

Read-only to clients: a requester cannot claim a service's key.

ticket_number.description:
TicketNumber is the human reference ("ticket #1042") — DB-generated
identity, global across tenants (see migration 000061).

can_retry.description:
Computed on read by Decorate, never stored. The server owns this policy:
a client that re-derives it from Status will get `expired` wrong (it is
retryable) and will conflate `verified` with being blocked.

rejection_scope.description:
RejectionScope names WHICH terminal state this is — ScopeVerification (this
inquiry failed, re-sendable) or ScopeCustomer (the provider rejected the
customer outright, nothing on our side lifts it). NULL/"" means the
provider never told us, which is every row written before migration 000093.

alerted_at.description:
AlertedAt stamps when this finding paged, so it pages once rather than every
pass. History is kept: a re-detected condition opens a NEW row, which is what
makes flapping visible instead of hidden behind one perpetually-open row.

details.description:
Details is the evidence: the numbers that produced the verdict (threshold,
authorization_keys, user_is_member, the two quorum ids). Present so "why is this
flagged" is answerable from the row alone, without re-reading the provider.

first_detected_at.description:
FirstDetectedAt is the dwell clock the worklist sorts by. Preserved across
passes — an upsert must never reset it, or a long-standing problem would look
new forever and nothing would ever appear old.

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is nil for a provider session — Privy owns that lifetime and
never tells us when it ends.

id.description: refresh-token family id, or a provider-session row id

kind.description:
Kind names the id space: "enforcer" for a refresh-token family, otherwise
the provider that owns the session ("privy").

is_discoverable.description:
IsDiscoverable controls whether this account appears to other members in
contact discovery (/contacts/suggestions, /contacts/lookup, /contacts/
resolve). It had no writer anywhere in the API: the column was stamped
once at account creation from the tenant's allow_user_discovery and could
never be changed, so "discovery is opt-out" was only true on paper.

Self-service by design — it is the subject's own privacy setting, and this
endpoint is already reachable by the owner (write on your own account is
the authz baseline). It cannot be used to become MORE visible than the
tenant permits: the tenant-wide allow_user_discovery gate is checked
independently on every discovery read, so a false there hides everyone
regardless of this flag.

key.description: full plaintext — shown once, never again

created_at.description:
CreatedAt is when the SESSION started, not when its current token was
minted. Rotation used to advance this, so a session refreshed every 15
minutes always reported itself as 15 minutes old.

current.description:
Current marks the session this request is being made from — the one the
caller must NOT revoke if they intend to stay signed in. Resolved from
whichever id space the caller is in: the access token's sid claim for an
enforcer session, the provider's sid for a Privy one. Still false for
every session when the credential carries neither (API key, portal link).

expires_at.description:
ExpiresAt is nil for a provider session. Privy owns that session's
lifetime and never tells us when it ends; reporting a guess on a security
surface would be worse than reporting nothing.

kind.description:
Kind names which id space this session lives in. "enforcer" is a
refresh-token family; "privy" is a session the PROVIDER owns, which a
client authenticating with a raw Privy bearer is the only kind it has.
Before 000092 those were invisible here, so the primary client's session
list was permanently empty — the endpoint existed and answered "none".

last_used_at.description:
LastUsedAt is the last refresh for an enforcer session, and the last time
the token was PRESENTED for a provider one (advanced by a throttled write,
so it lags by up to one interval). Nil only for an enforcer session that
has never rotated.

address.description:
Address is lower-cased. Every comparison against it must lower-case the
other side; EVM addresses are case-insensitive and the checksum casing a
wallet or QR code emits is not stable across sources.

phone.description: person's primary phone; filled only when persons is wired

tenant_id.description:
TenantID targets a tenant override (admin only — a tenant_admin is always
pinned to their own tenant). Empty = the system default (admin only).

group_type_id.description:
GroupTypeID classifies the group (optional). Must be a GLOBAL type or
one from the caller's tenant.

GroupTypeID: nil = unchanged, "" = clear, uuid = retag (same tenant rule
as CreateInput).

tenant_id.description:
TenantID targets a tenant-scoped type (admin only — a tenant_admin is
always pinned to their own tenant). Empty = GLOBAL for an admin, the
caller's own tenant for a tenant_admin (mirrors email templates).

home_place_id.description:
Home address — canonical, owned here (cybrid KYC + report-builder read it).
HomePlaceID references an enforcer-geo place; the rest is a denormalized
snapshot so /auth/me serves the address without a geo round-trip.

email_changed.description: verified flag was cleared; re-verify needed

id.description:
ID identifies the resource for logging and for custom policies that key
on it. It is NOT resolved to a stored row.

owner_id.description: OwnerID is the owning account. Required for an owner-baseline check.

tenant_id.description:
TenantID is the owning tenant. Required for any tenant-scoped grant —
including every admin-managed type. Omit it and the check is judged
against an empty tenant, not against the caller's.

contexts.description: Contexts is a free-form payload the policy may key on (size-capped).

policy_id.description:
PolicyID selects a stored policy; empty falls through to the built-in
static policy (HTTP parity with the gRPC Authorize).

user_id.description:
SubjectAccountID (user_id) evaluates on behalf of another account — the
caller must be able to read it. Empty = evaluate as the caller.

active.description: Active defaults to true on create; on update it is applied as given.

tenant_id.description:
TenantID targets a tenant-scoped policy (admin may target any tenant; a
tenant_admin is always pinned to their own). Empty = a global policy
(admin only).

TenantID is present only when Valid. A pointer, not a bare uuid.UUID:
that zero-valued to "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000" and shipped it
on every invalid-code lookup, so an unauthenticated visitor pasting a
typo'd share link got back a syntactically valid tenant id. A client that
reads tenant_id before checking valid would carry the nil UUID into a
join. omitempty on a [16]byte array does nothing, so the field has to be
nilable to be omitted at all.

config.description: non-nil replaces the config; omitted secrets are carried over

declaredTypes.description:
DeclaredTypes are the resource types the policy is authoritative for,
read from its own `declared_types` rule. Platform types are rejected
here rather than ignored later: a tenant claiming authority over
`account` must be told no, not silently overruled at evaluation.

error.description:
Error is why not, phrased for the person who wrote the policy — they
cannot see our logs and "compilation failed" tells them nothing.

ok.description: OK is whether the policy may be activated.

testsFailed.description: TestsRun and TestsFailed report the policy's own test_ rules.

testsRun.description: TestsRun and TestsFailed report the policy's own test_ rules.

web3_enabled.description:
Web3Enabled / MeteredSendsEnabled are the two web3 gates. They are validated
as a PAIR against their effective values, so turning web3 off while metering
is already on is refused just like turning metering on while web3 is off —
the same illegal state reached from either direction.

verification_status.description:
VerificationStatus is the KYC rollup bucket — verified | pending | failed
| none — decorated onto list rows, absent on payloads that do not resolve
it. NOT the same thing as ProfileCompleted, which is an admin-set
provisioner flag and says nothing about identity.

contact.description: scope to one counterparty (its account id)

created_after.description: RFC3339 window floor (match the badge read's floor)

account_phone.description: AccountPhone is persons.primary_phone — accounts carry no phone column.

auth_provider.description:
AuthProvider is the tenant's effective provider and the context for every
null below — a native or enterprise tenant has no Privy side at all.

email_matches_account.description:
EmailMatchesAccount is the field to read first. A Privy-linked address that
has drifted from accounts.email sends every login code to an inbox the user
no longer reads, and nothing else in the database exposes it. null — never
false — when either side is blank: "Privy holds no email" is a different
problem from "the emails disagree", and both values are in this body, so a
null always explains itself.

last_login_at.description:
LastLoginAt is EMPTY for every Privy-token user by construction, not by
accident. It ships anyway: seeing the blank next to a healthy Privy posture
is what stops the next reader taking it for "never logged in".

passkey_mfa.description:
PasskeyMfa is the same live posture GET /accounts/{id}/passkey-mfa serves,
folded in so a lockout ticket costs one request rather than three.

phone_matches_account.description:
PhoneMatchesAccount is the same comparison for the number, both sides
canonicalized so formatting is never reported as drift.

privy.description: Privy is null for an account with no Privy user.

tenant_id.description:
TenantID is the tenant actually read, which for a tenant-scoped caller is
always their own regardless of what they asked for.

email.description:
Email is the address the attempt was made with. Stored hashed and masked,
never in the clear.

event.description:
Event must be one of the closed set: otp_requested, otp_send_failed,
otp_verify_failed, login_failed.

tenant_code.description:
TenantCode names the tenant — the same handle the client already passes to
GET /auth/config, since a pre-auth caller has no other.

acknowledged.description:
Acknowledged defaults to true (POST /ack means "mark"); pass false to
clear. Idempotent set/clear, not a toggle.

custom_avatar_url.description:
CustomAvatarURL is this owner's private picture override for the contact —
a CDN URL previously returned by an enforcer-files image upload. Set on a
LINKED contact it shadows that person's own profile picture, for this owner
only; on a custom contact it is the only picture available. Must be https
and, when the deployment configures an allowlist, on an approved CDN host.

custom_wallet_address.description:
CustomWalletAddress is the pay-to wallet for a custom (off-platform)
contact — the QR-scan flow's payload. Previously ABSENT from this struct:
the client sent it, the server silently dropped it, and wallet-only
contacts landed unpayable and un-dedupable.

expected_payer_wallet.description:
ExpectedPayerWallet restricts funding to ONE wallet: a settlement from any
other payer will not confirm this fulfillment. Optional; omitted means
anyone may pay it, which is the normal case. Use it when the payer is the
point rather than a detail — a refund that must leave the merchant's
settlement wallet.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey de-duplicates this create. Optional, but strongly advised
for any client that can retry: pass the same key and a second call returns
the ORIGINAL fulfillment (200-shaped, same id) instead of minting a second
payment. Unique per tenant, 8..255 chars, and durable for the row's whole
life — a retry after the original settled still resolves to it.

sender_user_id.description:
SenderUserID addresses the payer by account id — used by the "request" flow
when the contact has no on-chain wallet on file. Optional: when unset, the
sender defaults to the caller (the "send" flow). Mutually optional with
sender_wallet.

scope.description:
Scope narrows the key, space-delimited, in the OAuth vocabulary:
enforcer:read | enforcer:write | enforcer:admin | policy:self |
enforcer:<tag>.<effect>. Omitted means unnarrowed for an unscoped
caller, and the caller's own scope for a scoped one.

tenant_id.description: admin only; tenant admins are forced to their own tenant

description.description: Description is free text stored in the wallet's metadata.

label.description: Label is the wallet's display name, mirrored to the provider. Max 100.

make_primary.description:
MakePrimary promotes the new wallet immediately, re-pointing the address
other users pay to.

email_verified.description: Verification badges — the flags, never the underlying identifiers.

name.description:
Name is the person's display name when set, which is what the picker
shows in preference to the account's first/last pair.

wallet_address.description:
WalletAddress is the primary address. Kept because discovery feeds the
send-destination picker; the VALUE is already public on-chain, unlike
everything dropped above.

version.description:
Version is the git revision this binary was built from, or "unknown" when
the build carries no stamp. Its ABSENCE is meaningful too: a response with
no version field is an image predating this endpoint, which is usually the
answer a deploy check wants.

authenticated_at.description:
authenticated_at / last_login_at update only on a fresh Login (not on token
refresh); last_active_at is the warm-path freshness signal (throttled).

groups.description:
Groups are the authz groups the caller belongs to, resolved to {id, slug,
name} so clients can gate on slug + display a label without a separate
lookup. No omitempty: always an array (NewMeData seeds []), so a groupless
account serializes as [] rather than null/absent.

kyc_verified.description:
No omitempty: a bool false must serialize so clients can distinguish
"not KYC-verified" from "field absent / older server".

passkey_mfa_verified_at.description:
PasskeyMfaVerifiedAt is the server-verified passkey MFA completeness
stamp (POST /auth/me/passkey/verify). Clients gate onboarding on this,
not on Privy's eventually-consistent client SDK arrays. NULL/absent =
never server-verified.

person.description: Canonical identity + auth context (nested; each carries its own id).

referral.description:
Referral is the caller's own affiliate/referral code (id + code), folded in
so the client doesn't need a separate GET /referrals/my-code on hydration.
Best-effort: omitted if the lookup/mint fails.

terms.description:
Terms posture — slim: one flat entry per current document (id + acceptance,
no document body) plus the mandatory gate. Enough to drive the onboarding
gate/badge; fetch full text from GET /terms/{id} or /auth/me/terms.
Best-effort: omitted if the terms lookup fails.

wallet_address.description:
WalletAddress is the account's PRIMARY wallet — the denormalized mirror of
account_wallets' primary row, which is what deposits, contact lookups and
every account-keyed read resolve to. Absent when the account holds none.

Deliberately just the address, and deliberately taken from the account row so
/auth/me stays a single query: this is the hydration path, and it is called on
every app open. The wallet's KIND and its signing posture are a different
question with a different cost — GET /me/wallets lists all of them with kind
and owner quorum, and GET /me/wallets/multisig reads the live posture from the
provider. A client that needs to know whether the primary is a co-signed 2-of-2
must ask one of those; this field only says which address is primary.

wallet_send_migration_required.description:
WalletSendMigrationRequired is true when this account holds a smart wallet
on a send-enforced tenant (a tenant_connections row carries the flag) that
hasn't yet had the mandatory app-key owner quorum attached. Set by the Me
handler (needs a connections lookup, so NewMeData can't compute it). The
PWA reads it here to prompt the one-time, user-authorized owner-change.
No omitempty: a false must serialize so clients distinguish "not required"
from "older server".

group_type_id.description:
GroupTypeID is the group's taxonomy, so a client can gate on "my groups
of type X" without a second call. Omitted for an untyped group.

A slug alone is already unambiguous WITHIN a tenant (uk_groups_tenant_slug
is on (tenant_id, slug), not (tenant_id, group_type_id, slug)), so a
consumer that knows its slugs up front does not need this field — it is
for the caller that wants to enumerate one taxonomy it does not have a
slug list for.

scopes.description:
Scopes REPLACES the ceiling: what is listed here is exactly what the
client may hold afterwards, no more and no less.

message.description:
Message states what did NOT change. Existing grants and issued tokens
keep the scope fixed at issue; the new ceiling applies from the next
/authorize consent and the next token exchange.

confidential.description:
Confidential separates the clients an admin minted, which can exchange
tokens, from the ones that registered themselves and cannot.

needs_stamp.description: NeedsStamp: enrolled on Privy, never stamped here — safe to backfill.

stamp_diverged.description: StampDiverged: stamped, but Privy no longer reports a backed enrollment.

primary_phone.description:
Phone lives on the person (persons.primary_phone) — surfaced here so
admin lists can show phone + its verification without a second read.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey, as on POST /fulfillments. A service has no /me list to
recover a lost create through, so this is how a retry finds the original.

payee_account_id.description:
PayeeAccountID is the account this request pays: creator, sender and
receiver all at once. Required.

amount_uoa.description: AmountUOA is minor units, at most what is still refundable. Required.

deadline_seconds.description:
DeadlineSeconds is how long the merchant has to pay it. 0 takes the
server's default.

idempotency_key.description:
IdempotencyKey makes a retry return the ORIGINAL refund instead of raising
a second one. Send the proposal id.

tx_hash.description:
TxHash is the mined transaction that paid the row: 0x + 64 hex. Case is
folded; it is stored lower-case.

body.example: I need help with my account.

source.description:
Source is an OPTIONAL stamp for program-filed tickets: "automated" marks
the ticket as filed by code (the PWA's Plaid auto-ticket), so the support
queue can hide it server-side (GET /tickets?source=support_contact)
instead of guessing from the subject. Omitted = support_contact (a
person). Any other value is a 400.

validation.description:
Validation is present on submit: whether the version may be activated,
and if not, why — phrased for the person who wrote the policy.

body.example: My payment to ACME was declined twice.

success.description: deprecated: token validity, NOT request success — read Valid

custom_avatar_url.description:
CustomAvatarURL replaces the picture override. Send "" to CLEAR it, which
falls a linked contact back to that person's own profile picture; omit the
field to leave it unchanged.

custom_wallet_address.description:
CustomWalletAddress registers the pay-to wallet on a CUSTOM contact — the
act that makes the contact payable, since send destinations derive from the
address book. Send "" to CLEAR it, which revokes that permission; omit to
leave unchanged. Rejected (400) on a linked contact, whose address is their
own account's active wallet.

username.description: account-scoped; applied to the caller's current account

needs_owner_migration.description:
NeedsOwnerMigration is true when the one-time user-authorized owner change
still has to happen for this wallet.

requires_both_signatures.description:
RequiresBothSignatures is the field a UI must render "protected" from, and
requires_server_cosign is NOT a substitute for it. The latter is also true
of an app-only quorum (the server signs alone — full custody) and of a
quorum whose app keys already meet the threshold, both of which would
display as "we co-sign your transactions" while meaning the opposite. This
field is true only when neither the user alone nor the server alone can
sign.

requires_server_cosign.description:
RequiresServerCosign is the question that matters: true means the user's
session alone can no longer sign, so the server must co-sign. It needs BOTH
an app key in the quorum AND threshold >= 2 — an app key at threshold 1 lets
the server sign but leaves the user able to sign alone too, which is
capability without enforcement.

resolved.description:
Resolved is false when the posture could not be read from the provider; the
fields above are then unknown rather than "not required".

signer_wallet_id.description:
SignerWalletID is the Privy wallet id whose owner quorum governs this
wallet — the id an owner change must be addressed to. For a smart wallet
this is the embedded EOA beneath it, since a smart wallet has no Privy
wallet id and no quorum of its own.

threshold.description:
Threshold is how many quorum members must sign; AuthorizationKeys counts
the app-held keys among them.

owner_quorum_id.description:
OwnerQuorumID is the Privy key quorum owning the wallet, present only when
the wallet was minted quorum-owned. Its presence tells a client that this
wallet cannot be signed for by the user's session alone — the app key is a
required co-signer — and the client needs the id itself to build the
authorization payload. Omitted for user-owned wallets, i.e. all of them
before wallet-send-enforcement is switched on for a tenant.

wallet_kind.description:
WalletKind is "smart" (the primary, paymaster-sponsored) or "embedded"
(a secondary EOA that pays its own gas). Clients use it to decide whether
to warn about gas before a send.

enforced.description:
Enforced is true when self-serve creation is capped at WorkspaceSlots on
this instance; false means the numbers are informational.

owned.description: Owned is how many live workspaces the caller owns.

plan_id.description:
PlanID is the workspace plan: personal | developer | business, or ""
when the caller has no plan.

workspace_slots.description: WorkspaceSlots is the effective number of workspaces the caller may own.
